page: Vultr vhf-4c-16gb is a virtual server instance within the High Frequency Compute family. It features an Intel x86_64 processor configured with 4 shared vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with Hyper-Threading enabled. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled and consists of a 384 GB NVMe SSD. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, and no dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results indicate average performance across several standard compute workloads. The instance achieved a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 2411.16 and a multi-core score of 8740.87. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached read bandwidth is strong at 497.33 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the lower tier at 35.47 GB/sec and 17.49 GB/sec respectively. Cryptographic and compression tests, such as single-threaded gzip compression and Passmark CPU encryption, also demonstrate weaker relative performance. However, Redis SET operations perform steadily at 6.0 million operations per second.

Because this instance utilizes shared CPU allocation, resource contention may affect sustained high-compute workloads, representing a key tradeoff for its hardware class. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a balanced resource density of memory and NVMe storage relative to its shared-vCPU profile. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads, lightweight database operations, text processing, and basic web serving where continuous maximum CPU utilization is not required.
